title: Degradation record — v1.0
description: plan.md §4's second worked example, chainlink #25. One per degraded cluster at specs/_closure/<cluster>.degradation.json -- the same directory as the closure profile it sits beside, distinguished by the filename suffix exactly as plan.md's own example writes it. 'A declared state, not a failure, on the same footing as protocol debt': a cluster that cannot meet every closure condition is not thereby unreleasable, it is releasable with a named, reviewed, tracked shortfall and an explicit ceiling. What a degradation record can excuse is bounded by its own vocabulary: failed_conditions is an enum of closure-profile CONDITION keys, so it can never excuse a missing proof, an unsatisfied requirement, an unsupported dependency, or a failed bridge -- those are absences of evidence, not declared ceilings, and scripts/gate_g14.py keeps blocking on them with a degradation record present.

cluster.description: Must equal the filename stem with the '.degradation' suffix removed (G1b, scripts/validate_closure.py): specs/_closure/analysis-configuration.degradation.json declares cluster 'analysis-configuration', and names the same cluster its closure profile does.

failed_conditions.description: Exactly the condition keys of docs/closure-profile-schema.json's `conditions` block. A record may only excuse conditions it actually names, and G14 rejects a record naming a condition that in fact holds (G17: 'profile bits inconsistent with degradation record') -- a stale excuse is as misleading as a missing one, and would keep a cluster reading as degraded after the gap closed.

affected_edges.description: The boundary_ids (or bridge_ids) the shortfall actually lands on -- plan.md §4's own field. Non-empty by construction: a degradation with no located edge is an unfalsifiable claim about the whole cluster.

ceiling.description: The strongest thing this cluster may claim while degraded, from plan.md §3's Ceiling column and §8.1's vocabulary. CG1 (cross-verifier composition) is `harness-tested`; CG3 (generics under Kani) is `per-instantiation`; CG5 (non-falsifiable assumptions) is `human-risk-acceptance`. Never a verification-method value -- a ceiling is a limit on the claim, not a claim to have run something.

capability_gap.description: The capability gap from plan.md §3 this degradation instantiates, when it instantiates one. Optional: a shortfall can be ordinary project debt rather than a permanent capability gap, and forcing every record into a CG bucket would misrepresent the fixable ones as permanent.

tracking_issue.description: e.g. chainlink:713. plan.md §3's response to every capability gap is 'degradation record + tracking issue' -- the record says what was accepted, the issue is where the accepting stops being permanent. Same shape as a work-package manifest's own trusted_assumptions[].assumption_ref.tracking_issue.

review.description: plan.md §7.2's human checkpoint: 'closure-profile/degradation-record acceptance'. Accepting a ceiling is a risk decision and never a mechanical one.
